title: Effect of intercropping on crop yield compared to sole cropping
research_question: Does intercropping (growing two or more crops simultaneously in the same field) increase crop yield compared to sole cropping / monoculture?

population.description: Field crops (cereals, legumes, vegetables) grown in intercropping systems

intervention.description: Intercropping (strip, row, relay, mixed) with any companion crop

comparator.description: Sole cropping / monoculture of the same crop
comparator.definition: The same crop grown alone (monoculture / sole crop) at equivalent density or area

primary.description: Crop yield (grain yield, biomass, total yield) of the primary crop or combined system
primary.direction_of_interest: positive (intercropping expected to increase total yield)

intervention: Intercropping (strip, row, relay, mixed) with any companion crop
control: Sole cropping / monoculture of the same crop
primary_outcomes: Crop grain yield or biomass per unit area (kg/ha, Mg/ha, t/ha)
important_moderators: Primary crop species (maize, wheat, sorghum, millet, rice, barley)
Companion crop species (soybean, cowpea, common bean, groundnut, pea, faba bean)
Intercropping type (strip, row, relay, mixed/additive, replacement)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of EACH crop species separately in the intercrop AND the corresponding sole crop control
2. Treatment = crop yield UNDER intercropping; Control = same crop yield under sole cropping/monoculture
3. If LER is reported, extract it as a separate outcome row
6. Record both the primary and companion crop species
7. Record intercropping arrangement type (strip, row, relay, mixed)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is yield UNDER INTERCROPPING, Control is yield UNDER SOLE CROPPING
Some papers report yields of BOTH crops in the intercrop - extract each separately vs its own sole crop control
Do NOT confuse intercropping with crop rotation - intercropping is SIMULTANEOUS growing
Relay intercropping has temporal overlap but crops are not identical in timing - still counts as intercropping
LER > 1 means intercropping is MORE productive per unit land than monocultures
Some papers report 'partial LER' for each crop - extract both partial and total LER if available
Additive vs replacement designs differ - in additive, intercrop density is higher than sole crop

search.seed_papers_description: Yu et al. 2015 (Agronomy for Sustainable Development, 100-study meta-analysis), Li et al. 2020 (Field Crops Research), Martin-Guay et al. 2018

inclusion_criteria: Primary field experiment comparing intercropping vs sole cropping/monoculture
Reports yield or biomass data for at least one crop (numeric means)
Includes both intercropping treatment and sole crop control
Crops grown simultaneously in the same field (not rotation)
exclusion_criteria: No yield or biomass data reported
Only reports LER without underlying yield data
Agroforestry with tree crops only (no annual field crops)

benchmark.source: Yu et al. 2015 (Agronomy for Sustainable Development 35:767-778)

published_pooled_effect.notes: LER = 1.22 across 100 studies; 22% more total land needed for monocultures to match intercrop output. Also supported by Li et al. 2020 finding similar magnitudes.
